subject: Renewal proposal: premium SLA + capacity bump for Kite Health
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lawson <emma@kitehealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal: premium SLA + capacity bump for Kite Health

Hi Emma —

Our records show Kite Health's annual contract is up for renewal on 2026-07-15. Given the increased production traffic and your Q3 launch, I wanted to propose a renewal path that upgrades you to Redwood Premium SLA and reserves a modest capacity bump to cover the new patient routing workload. High-level proposal: 

- Premium SLA: guaranteed 95th/99th latency SLOs at the panel sizes you shared (95th < 180ms, 99th < 400ms) with monthly measurement and credits if exceeded.
- Reserved capacity: add a 20% committed buffer on top of current baseline (can be adjusted after a 30-day canary).
- Burst credits: one-time pool of 250k tokens for traffic spikes during onboarding/launch.
- Commercials: 15% uplift on base usage rate + a per-token rebate above committed volume. We can surface a few pricing alternatives depending on term length (12 vs 24 months).

I've attached a short SLA proposal and an SLO matrix that maps our metrics to your routes. If this sounds promising, can we schedule a 30-minute walkthrough next week with your platform lead and procurement to align on pilot scope and procurement timing?

Attachments: Redwood_Premium_SLA_Proposal_2026-06-18.pdf (proposal), SLO_matrix_kitehealth.xlsx (route-level targets)

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Emma Lawson <emma@kitehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@kitehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: premium SLA + capacity bump for Kite Health

Thanks Karthik —

Appreciate the proactive proposal. A couple of quick questions before we loop procurement:

1) Can you confirm the precise numeric targets that would be contractually guaranteed for 95th and 99th latency? We need the language to be deterministic for our SRE team.
2) What is the expected incremental cost for the 20% reserved buffer (monthly $ / committed tokens)?
3) Our VP of Platform will want a short pilot that validates tail latency for our worst-case route. Is the 30-day canary paid or complimentary?

Procurement timeline is tight — they ideally need final terms by 2026-07-05. Also, please include a runbook and SOC2 evidence for our security review.

— Emma
Emma Lawson
Head of Platform, Kite Health
emma@kitehealth.com | +1 (206) 555-0108

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lawson <emma@kitehealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: premium SLA + capacity bump for Kite Health

Emma —

Thanks for the questions; cc'ing Camila (CS) and Monica (Pricing) so we can align on a single reply and get procurement what they need. Initial answers: 

- Contract SLOs (draft language): "Redwood warrants that for the covered routes the 95th percentile inference latency will not exceed 180ms and the 99th percentile will not exceed 400ms as measured over the full calendar month, subject to the traffic profile agreed in the SLO matrix. If Redwood fails to meet these targets for two consecutive months, customer will be eligible for service credits as defined in Section 5."

- Pricing for the 20% reserved buffer: estimated incremental commit of $4,200/month (this is a placeholder; Monica will run final numbers against last 12 months usage and propose 12- vs 24-month term discounts).

- 30-day canary/pilot: we can offer the first 14 days complimentary (no added commit) to validate integration and tail latency. The remaining 16 days, if you choose to continue the canary under reserve, would pro-rate against the committed buffer. The pilot will include a focused telemetry bundle and weekly checkpoints with our SRE.

Action items I propose:
1) Camila to draft a short pilot test plan (routes, load profile, success criteria).
2) Monica to provide a pricing worksheet for 12 vs 24 month terms and the impact of the reserved buffer.
3) Karthik / Camila to schedule a 30-min alignment with your Platform and Procurement next Tue or Wed (6/23 or 6/24).

Cc: Camila, Monica — please weigh in and drop the pilot doc and pricing worksheet into the shared drive link.

Thanks,
Karthik

Karthik / Camila / Monica —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. VP wants a one-week focused pilot to validate tail latency on the "patient-match" route under worst-case concurrency; after that they will move forward with final approval. Two additional asks: 

- Please share SOC2 Type II evidence and the ops runbook for incident response and escalation (we need to attach to the procurement packet).
- We will need the pilot test plan and a signed mutual NDA addendum for telemetry sharing (we can draft the short addendum).

Can you confirm availability for a joint test kick-off call on Wed 2026-06-24 at 10:00 PT? If you can provide the pilot doc and the SOC2 stub beforehand (by EOD Tue 6/23) that would keep procurement on track.

If we can get the pilot completed and results validated by 7/2, procurement can finalize terms by your 7/5 target.

— Emma
